QuestionText: Two figures are congruent if they have the same shape and size
Explanation: Congruent figures are identical in shape and size.

QuestionText: SAS needs two equal sides and the included angle
Options: D) Only if all sides equal
Explanation: SAS: two sides and the angle between them.

QuestionText: SSS needs ___ equal sides
Explanation: SSS needs all three pairs of corresponding sides equal.

QuestionText: In ASA, the side must be between the two equal angles
Explanation: ASA: the side is included between the two angles.

QuestionText: RHS applies only to right-angled triangles
Explanation: RHS requires a right angle, hypotenuse, and one leg.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC congruent to PQR: vertex B corresponds to
Explanation: Correspondence A-P, B-Q, C-R.

QuestionText: CPCT means Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are equal
Explanation: CPCT: all corresponding parts (sides and angles) of congruent triangles are equal.

QuestionText: SSA is NOT a valid congruence criterion
Explanation: Two different triangles can satisfy SSA: not a valid criterion.

QuestionText: AAS criterion uses two angles and a non-included side
Explanation: AAS: two angles and any side not between them.

QuestionText: Two congruent triangles always have equal areas
Explanation: Congruent triangles are identical so areas are equal.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC congruent to DEF: AB=DE=5, angle B=angle E=60, BC=EF=7. Criterion?
Explanation: Two sides and included angle equal: SAS.

QuestionText: Two equilateral triangles with side 6 cm are congruent by
Explanation: All three sides equal: SSS.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC congruent to DEF means angle A equals angle
Explanation: A-D, B-E, C-F correspondence.

QuestionText: Congruence is an equivalence relation: reflexive, symmetric, and transitive
Explanation: All three properties hold: it is an equivalence relation.

QuestionText: How many standard congruence criteria exist for triangles
Explanation: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS: five criteria.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC with AB=AC, D midpoint of BC. ABD and ACD congruent by
Explanation: AB=AC, BD=DC, AD=AD (common): SSS.

QuestionText: Two right triangles with equal hypotenuse and one leg: criterion
Explanation: RHS: right angle, hypotenuse, side.

QuestionText: Isosceles triangle: angle bisector from apex creates two congruent triangles by
Explanation: Equal sides, equal bisected angles, common side: SAS.

QuestionText: Parallelogram ABCD diagonal AC: triangles ABC and CDA congruent by
Explanation: AB=CD, BC=DA, AC=CA (common): SSS.

QuestionText: Triangle PQR and STU: angle P=angle S=90 hyp PR=SU PQ=ST. Criterion
Explanation: Right angle, hypotenuse equal, side equal: RHS.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC congruent to QPR. AB corresponds to side
Explanation: A-Q, B-P, C-R. AB corresponds to QP.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC congruent to DEF: angle A=50 angle F=70. Find angle B
Explanation: A-D, B-E, C-F. Angle C=70 (=F). Angle B=180-50-70=60.

QuestionText: Square ABCD diagonal BD: triangles ABD and CBD congruent by
Explanation: AB=CB, angle ABD=angle CBD, BD=BD: SAS.

QuestionText: Triangle ABD congruent to CBD implies angle ABD=angle CBD by
Explanation: By CPCT corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal.

QuestionText: Two triangles with all three equal angles are similar but NOT necessarily congruent
Explanation: AAA gives similarity (equal angles) but sides could be scaled differently.

QuestionText: Triangle PQR congruent to XYZ and XYZ congruent to LMN implies triangle PQR congruent to LMN
Explanation: Congruence is transitive.

QuestionText: In perpendicular bisector proof: triangles RMA and RMB where M is midpoint. Congruent by
Explanation: RM=RM, angle RMA=angle RMB=90, MA=MB: SAS.

QuestionText: Triangle PQR and DEF: angle P=angle D angle Q=angle E PQ=DE. Criterion
Explanation: Two angles and included side: ASA.

QuestionText: Triangle ABD and PQS: BD corresponds to
Explanation: A-P, B-Q, D-S. BD corresponds to QS.

QuestionText: In triangle ABC and DBC, AB=DB, AD is common, angle ABC=angle DBC. Congruent by
Explanation: AB=DB, angle ABC=angle DBC, BC=BC: SAS.

QuestionText: If AB=AC in triangle ABC, the altitude from A is also the median. This is because triangles ABD and ACD are congruent by
Explanation: Angle ADB=Angle ADC=90, AB=AC (hypotenuse), AD=AD: RHS.

Explanation: Congruent triangles have equal areas.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC with sides 3,4,5 and triangle PQR with sides 3,4,5 are
Explanation: All three sides equal: SSS.

QuestionText: Two squares with the same side length are
Explanation: Same side length means all four sides equal in both: congruent.

QuestionText: In triangle ABD congruent to triangle CBD, angle B in ABD = angle B in CBD. Both equal 40 degrees. Find angle ABC
Explanation: Angle ABC = angle ABD + angle CBD = 40+40 = 80 degrees.

QuestionText: Medians of two congruent triangles are
Explanation: By CPCT all corresponding measurements including medians are equal.

QuestionText: Altitudes of two congruent triangles are
Explanation: Congruent triangles: all corresponding altitudes are equal.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC: AB=6 BC=8 angle B=90. Triangle DEF: DE=6 EF=8 angle E=90. Congruent by
Explanation: AB=DE=6, BC=EF=8, included angle B=E=90: SAS.

QuestionText: In rhombus ABCD diagonal AC: triangles ABC and CDA are congruent because all sides of a rhombus are
Explanation: All sides of rhombus equal: AB=BC=CD=DA. With common diagonal AC: SSS.

QuestionText: Triangle ABC congruent to FED. Then BC corresponds to
Explanation: A-F, B-E, C-D. BC corresponds to ED.

QuestionText: In proving two triangles congruent by RHS we need: right angle, hypotenuse, and
Explanation: RHS: Right angle, Hypotenuse, one Side (leg).

QuestionText: If triangle ABD congruent to triangle PQR and PQ=7, AB=
Explanation: A-P, B-Q, D-R. AB corresponds to PQ=7.

Explanation: Triangles PAQ and PAR: PA=PA, angle PAQ=angle PAR=90, PQ=PR: RHS gives AQ=AR.

QuestionText: Two circles are congruent if their radii are
Explanation: Congruent circles have equal radii.

QuestionText: If all three sides of triangle A equal all three sides of triangle B the triangles are
Explanation: SSS guarantees congruence: no need to check angles.

QuestionText: Triangle PQR: PQ=5 QR=8 PR=7. Triangle XYZ: XY=5 YZ=8 XZ=7. These triangles are
Explanation: All three sides match: SSS congruence.

QuestionText: Congruence of triangles was first formally established by
Explanation: Euclid formally established triangle congruence criteria in his Elements.

QuestionText: Which is a valid congruence test?
Explanation: AAS is valid. SSA, AAA, ASS are not sufficient for congruence.

QuestionText: If two triangles are congruent their corresponding altitudes altitudes are in ratio
Explanation: Congruent means identical so corresponding altitudes are equal: ratio 1:1.

QuestionText: Angle bisectors of isosceles triangle from equal base angles create congruent triangles by
Explanation: Equal base angles halved: equal half-angles, equal opposite sides, common altitude base. AAS.
